extracted.intended_audience: teachers, teacher-educators, school administrators, and students of pedagogy
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and evaluating classroom instruction and school organization to foster pupils' reflective (inquiry-based) thinking — i.e., activities that produce genuine problems, supply appropriate data, elicit pupil-generated ideas, and require testing by action. Emphasis is on method integrated with subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thinking as inquiry (tentative, risky, experimental)
rubrics_metrics.description: Thinking is a process of inquiry, of looking into things, of investigating; conclusions are tentative or hypothetical and must be tested by consequences — "all thinking involves a risk".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instruction should treat thinking as conjecture-and-test rather than as dogmatic assertion; learning activities should allow hypotheses to be formed and verified. Anti-pattern: presenting answers as final truths without opportunities for testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reflective experience — perplexity/doubt (sense of problem)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reflective experience begins with perplexity, confusion, or doubt caused by an incomplete situation whose full character is not yet determined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lessons should present situations that generate genuine uncertainty to stimulate inquiry. Anti-pattern: purely routine tasks that produce no doubt or perplexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reflective experience — conjectural anticipation (tentative interpretation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reflective experience includes a conjectural anticipation — a tentative interpretation attributing tendencies to given elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage students to form tentative explanations or predictions from observed data rather than only recall facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reflective experience — careful survey and analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Reflective experience requires a careful survey (examination, inspection, exploration, analysis) of all attainable considerations to define and clarify the problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teach students systematic observation and analysis skills; provide time and tasks that require comprehensive examination of conditions. Scoring note: depth and accuracy of survey distinguish reflective thinking from trial-and-error.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reflective experience — elaboration of hypothesis
rubrics_metrics.description: Reflective experience involves elaboration of the tentative hypothesis to make it more precise and consistent with a wider range of facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require students to refine and make hypotheses more precise in light of additional evidence; reward iterative improvement rather than one-off answers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reflective experience — testing by action (application)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reflective experience culminates in taking a stand upon the hypothesis as a plan of action and applying it to test whether anticipated consequences follow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete opportunities to apply ideas (experiments, projects) so that consequences test their validity. Anti-pattern: hypothetical discussion with no real-world testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial stage must be experience (empirical situation as initiation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The initial stage of thinking is experience: instruction must begin from an actual empirical situation — trying to do something and noting the interaction — not from abstract ready-made material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin lessons with hands-on or situational activities tied to real-life contexts. Avoid attempting to cultivate thinking in isolation from experience (e.g., immediate presentation of adult intellectual distinctions without concrete handling).

rubrics_metrics.name: Problems must be genuine (not mock or imposed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish genuine problems (naturally suggested by situation/personal experience) from simulated problems created solely for instruction; ask whether the question 'naturally suggests itself' or is 'aloof.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the two discriminating questions provided: (a) Does the question naturally arise from a situation? (b) Is it the pupil's own problem or merely the teacher/textbook's requirement? Reject problems that exist only to elicit an answer for grading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problems must be the pupil's problem (personal ownership)
rubrics_metrics.description: A pupil's problem should be his own, not simply the teacher's or textbook's problem turned into an exercise for marks or promotion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design tasks that engage pupils' personal interests or responsibilities so they feel ownership. Anti-pattern: tasks whose sole aim is to satisfy external school conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of problem — new yet connected
rubrics_metrics.description: A problem should present something new (uncertain/problematic) while remaining sufficiently connected with existing habits to call out effective response — not routine or capricious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose problems that challenge but do not overwhelm; include familiar elements ('luminous familiar spots') from which students can draw suggestions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of data/resources (facts, experiences, observations)
rubrics_metrics.description: To think effectively one must have experiences or data to furnish resources for coping with the difficulty — 'the material of thinking is not thoughts, but actions, facts, events, and the relations of things.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure students have appropriate facts, observations, and experiences available (via memory, observation, reading, communication). Anti-pattern: asking students to 'think things out for themselves' without supplying necessary material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance sources of information (observation, reading, communication)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use memory, observation, reading, and communication as avenues for supplying data in proportions suited to the specific problem; avoid excessive dependence on one mode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rely on observation when direct perception adds value; use reading and communication to supplement personal experience. Beware excessive reliance on sense-presentations or on others providing ready-made solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid supplying ready-made solutions — encourage adaptation
rubrics_metrics.description: Teachers/books must not supply ready-made solutions; students should adapt and apply material to the question for themselves rather than receive ready answers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide material that students must interpret and apply. Anti-pattern: teacher supplies full solutions that remove opportunity for student inference and invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ideas as creative projections (invention from familiar materials)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ideas/inferences are creative — projections beyond given data; originality lies in putting familiar materials to new uses or contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foster inventiveness by asking students to recontextualize familiar facts; reward novel uses of ordinary elements rather than fanciful novelty disconnected from data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learner-generated ideas — idea must be realized by student
rubrics_metrics.description: No thought can be conveyed as an idea from one person to another; the learner must wrestle with conditions and generate ideas himself; the teacher's role is to provide conditions and participate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure activities so pupils discover or construct ideas through engagement; teacher acts as co-learner and facilitator rather than sole presenter of ideas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application/testing confers meaning (practice must be intellectual)
rubrics_metrics.description: Application of ideas in real situations tests them and confers full meaning; practice should have an intellectual quality rather than merely fixing skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design practice tasks that require intellectual judgment and testing of ideas in context, not merely repetitive skill drills for rote performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide active pursuits to reproduce life situations
rubrics_metrics.description: Schools should be equipped with laboratories, shops, gardens, dramatizations, plays, and games to reproduce situations of life and enable acquisition and application of ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where possible use hands-on, constructive activities; ensure such activities are used to elicit thought and not only to develop bodily skill or serve narrow utilitarian ends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interconnection and continuity across lessons/subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Processes of instruction are unified in the degree they center on production of thinking; best teaching systematically leads students to use earlier lessons to understand current ones and to interrelate subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid treating each lesson as an independent whole; cultivate habitual attitudes of finding points of contact across lessons and subjects. Scoring note: coherence across a unit indicates stronger educative design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject storage-only knowledge; treat knowledge as working capital
rubrics_metrics.description: Knowledge should function as working capital for inquiry and action; accumulation for reproduction is inimical to educative development — rote information 'swamps thinking.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessments and activities should evaluate use of knowledge in problem-solving and application rather than mere reproduction. Anti-pattern: emphasizing memory-for-exam over use-in-context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of subject matter and method (teacher expertise)
rubrics_metrics.description: Method and subject matter are not separate; pedagogy divorced from content is false — teachers must have profound and accurate acquaintance with the subject to teach method effectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate teaching by both methodological soundness and depth of subject knowledge. Anti-pattern: applying abstract 'methods of mind' without grounding in the specific subject content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of materials and arrangements to generate real problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Physical equipment and arrangements of the schoolroom must supply material, appliances, and opportunities for doing things, otherwise real situations that generate problems will be absent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest in materials and opportunities for active engagement (more 'stuff' and appliances); pedagogical improvement alone cannot fully substitute for lack of material conditions.
